cluster_name: Pezeshkian delivers first UNGA address since US-Israel-Iran war began
event_summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the 81st UN General Assembly on September 23, 2026, in his first speech there since the US and Israel launched the Iran war. The address followed Trump's UNGA warning the day before that he was choosing between annihilating Iran and making a peace deal.
tldr: The most striking editorial divergence is in how outlets assign agency for the conflict: AFP/France 24 EN describes Pezeshkian's UNGA appearance as 'his first speech at the world body since the US and Israel launched the Iran war,' explicitly naming the US and Israel as initiators in a wire-service headline. Chinese state outlet CGTN is the only English-language source to publish IRGC military counter-threats at length — including spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi vowing to 'change the geography of the war' — a framing entirely absent from Western coverage. Iran's own state agency IRNA runs purely logistical dispatches (arrival date, speech scheduling) with no mention of Trump's annihilation threat, while anti-regime Iran International leads with Pezeshkian being 'squeezed at home' over whether to seek a direct Trump meeting or strike a defiant tone. French-language AFP focuses on possible Trump-Teheran dialogue announced the prior day, the most diplomatically optimistic framing among any outlet in the cluster; Southeast Asian and East African outlets follow suit, treating the visit as arriving 'amid hopes for diplomacy.'

frames.sub_frame: ongoing US-Israel-Iran war and mutual annihilation threats

outlet_exclusive_vocab_highlights.what_it_reveals: CGTN is the only outlet to name IRGC spokesperson Mohebbi and quote his 'change the geography of war' threat at length; 'september' reflects CGTN's dateline-heavy prose referencing the SCO Summit context.
Fox uniquely frames the event as two leaders converging on NYC and foregrounds US restrictions on Iran's delegation — a sovereignty-and-restriction angle absent from all other outlets.

French-language coverage is structurally separated from the English cluster; 'attendu' (anticipated/awaited) signals anticipatory framing, and 'négociations avec' points toward dialogue rather than confrontation.
East African coverage picks up and foregrounds Pezeshkian's pre-departure vow to 'firmly defend' Iran's positions — a defiance-posture framing, the exact phrase no other outlet headlines.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: Turkish President Erdogan used his UNGA address to raise the Kashmir issue; Hindustan Times' live blog records this as a separate speaking slot, suggesting Turkish press tracked Erdogan's own speech rather than the Iran-Trump dynamic.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Headline assigns war-start agency to the US and Israel — 'first time since US, Israel launched Iran war' — an explicitly causal framing in a wire-service title.

Only outlet to carry IRGC counter-threat language at length: Mohebbi vows to 'change the geography of the war' and deploy 'new weapons with new capabilities'; absent from all Western-country coverage.

Leads entirely with Pezeshkian's domestic political bind — competing factions pressing for Trump diplomacy or defiance — treating Iranian internal politics as the primary story over the war or the speech.
Focuses on US restrictions imposed on Iran's UNGA delegation movements — a logistical-sovereignty angle absent from all other outlets including IRNA.
Both IRNA dispatches are purely logistical (arrival date, speech scheduling); neither references Trump's annihilation threat or the ongoing war — a conspicuous omission by the official state agency.

French-language coverage centres on Trump's day-prior announcement of possible renewed dialogue ('reprise du dialogue avec Téhéran') rather than the annihilation threat — the most diplomatically optimistic Western framing in the cluster.
Only outlet to frame Pezeshkian's arrival as 'amid hopes for diplomacy' in the headline without qualification — neutral Southeast Asian framing furthest from the war register dominant elsewhere.

Frames Iran's UNGA participation alongside Ukraine and Syria as a routine 'second day of General Debate' — the flattest, most procedural framing of the three conflict-country speeches, notably de-escalatory.

bottom_line: Across 11 outlets and 11 countries, the dominant frame is military threat — Trump's annihilation ultimatum and IRGC counter-threats — but outlets diverge sharply on whether the UNGA encounter is a war milestone or a diplomatic opening. The most telling editorial gap: Iran's state agency IRNA runs purely procedural coverage ignoring Trump's threat entirely, while Chinese state media CGTN is the only outlet to amplify Iranian military counter-threats at length, foregrounding a war-continuation posture that Western and Gulf press largely bracket.
